seeded.description: The committed seed replayed through the real learning policy. This is the state a reviewer sees after `make seed`, so most application cases run against it.

empty.description: No memories at all. Used for learning cases (so what gets learned is attributable to the case's own observations) and for the no-memory application cases.

seeded_ambiguous_kiwi.description: Seed plus a SECOND confirmed memory that also answers to the sound 'kiwi' — a client called Kiwee alongside the product Kivi. Two equally good answers for one span is genuine ambiguity, and the system should abstain and say so rather than pick the marginally higher score (taxonomy N12).

manual_memories.gloss: a client, unrelated to the Kivi product
manual_memories.excerpt: added so that two memories compete for one sound

seeded_kivi_deleted.description: Seed, then the Kivi memory is deleted by the user. Deletion must take effect immediately: the word must stop being corrected (taxonomy N9).

seeded_sumeet_superseded.description: Seed, then 'Sumeet' is superseded by 'Sumit' — the person changed their mind about their own spelling. The new form must win, the old form must now itself be corrected, and the old memory must remain inspectable (taxonomy N10, brief section 13).

seeded_kivi_candidate.description: Seed, then the Kivi memory is demoted to candidate. Candidate memories are visible but inert: weak evidence must not change text (taxonomy N11).

holdout_persona.description: A DIFFERENT person's vocabulary, taught from scratch by its own observations. None of these words, wrong forms or contexts appear in the seed or in the dev split, so this scenario detects tuning to the development data.
